the decreased expression of CD 59, a membrane‐associated complement regulator, on T cells in acute Epstein–Barr Virus (EBV) induced infectious mononucleosus (IM) may be related to activation‐inducede cell death (apoptosis) of mature T cells.

the CD59 antigen is a membrane‐associated complement‐regulating protein, and that its decreased expression on activated CD8+ lymphocytes in acute infectious mononucelosis may be associated with the activation‐induced apoptosis of CD8+ T lymphocytes.

the expression of the complement‐regulatory protein CD59 on T cells in IM and its possible role in activation‐induced apoptosis.

the role of CD59 in the immunoregulation of IM.

decreased expression of HRF20/CD59 on T cells is a marker of T cell activation and that decreased expression of the CD59 antigen on activated T cells is a risk factor for apoptosis of activated T cells in acute IM.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the decreased CD59 on activated CD8 T cells may be one of the mechanisms that cause CD8 T cell death in IM, and the CD59 on activated T cells is one of the important factors that protect the cells from activation‐induced apoptosis.

decreased expression of HRF20 (a complement regulatory protein) on activated CD8+ cells is a possible mechanism for activation‐induced death of CD8+ T lymphocytes in EBV‐induced infectious mono‐nucleosis.
CD59 may play a role in the regulation of apoptosis in activated CD8+ cells in IM patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that

CD8+ T lymphocytes are more susceptible to complement‐mediated lysis in IM patients than healthy volunteers, and that the decreased expression of CD8+ T‐cell CD59 may be involved in the susceptibility.
the decreased expression of CD8+ T‐cell CD59 in acute IM may be a useful marker for predicting the susceptibility of activated T cells to apoptosis.
CD59 may be a marker for the activation status of CD8+ T lymphocytes.
